PION is free software in that you will not be charged money to use it, but there are some restrictions as to what you are permitted to do with it. The following restrictions largely follow the BSD licence, but with a couple of additions.

CONDITIONS OF USE AND REDISTRIBUTION¶

1. Redistributions of source code must reproduce this copyright notice, this list of conditions and disclaimers, unchanged and in its entirety (i.e. all of the text in this licence file).

3. 4. If you modify PION, you must clearly state this in publications arising from simulations using a modified version of the code. Furthermore, you must state clearly what modifications you have made, providing enough information for another computational astrophysicist to reproduce your results with reasonable effort.

5. PION, and any codes derived from it or using any of its source code, may not under any circumstances be used for weapons research and/or military research, including but not limited to modelling of weapons explosions and the evolution of associated blast waves, without explicit written permission from the authors, including handwritten signature.

6. In publications which use PION, or a modified version of PION, or components of PION incorporated into a new code, you agree to cite at least one of the relevant papers describing PION and its components:

  • Mackey & Lim (2010,MNRAS,403,714) for hydrodynamics and raytracing plus photoionisation,
  • Mackey & Lim (2011,MNRAS,412,2079) for photoionisation with magnetohydrodynamics,
  • Mackey (2012,A&A,539,A147) for updated explicit photoionisation algrithm.
  • Dhanoa, Mackey & Yates (2014,MNRAS,444,2085) for metal-free chemistry.
